subject: Re: Commitment re-balance & renewal uplift cap — Olympus Health

From: Olivia Park <procurement@olympus-health.com>

Cc: Miles Herrera <finance@olympus-health.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing + potential commit increase

Hi Ben,

We’re starting renewal discussions for our enterprise agreement (current commit: $480k/year) and exploring whether to move to a larger commit for calendar 2027. Two specific asks from my side:

1) If we increase committed spend by ~30% (to roughly $624k/year), what per-token discount tiers can Redwood offer versus our current rates? Please include any volume bands and effective per-token pricing you would apply.

2) Our finance team needs to understand renewal uplift limits and how you treat mid-term right-sizing. Specifically: are there contractual uplift caps year-over-year? Is there a cap on allowed increases to committed spend at renewal (we have seen providers limit uplift to ~20% without reprocurement)? Also, if we underutilize the new commit, do you provide credits / rollover or a wash?

Can you share a short write-up and an updated pricing table? We’d like to present options to procurement + finance next week.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Olympus Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal pricing + potential commit increase

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear asks. Quick reply while I pull the updated numbers:

High level answers:
- Yes, we have volume-based per-token discounts that improve with commit tiers. I’ll attach a simple table comparing your current tier to a +30% commit and show blended per-token rates.
- We do not lock customers into punitive uplift escalation; our standard renewal policy includes an annual uplift cap (contractually negotiated) — for customers on enterprise contracts we typically limit list-price changes to a single-digit percentage or negotiate an explicit uplift cap. That said, uplift caps and re-tiering rules are a contract negotiation point for enterprise deals.
- For underutilization, we offer a mix of options: limited rollover for up to one quarter (for predictable usage variance), and the ability to right-size the commit at renewal with pro-rated crediting for unused committed dollars (subject to minimum term constraints).

I’m looping in Lauren and Jordan to confirm the numbers and to propose two structured options (Conservative: small uplift cap + flexible rollover; Aggressive: larger discount bands tied to usage guardrails and a 15% uplift cap). Will follow up with a short deck and pricing table by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Olympus renewal — pricing options for Olivia

Team — drafting two options to send to Olympus. Need quick calibration on legality/precedent and margin hit: please review below and reply inline.

Option A — Conservative- Commit: $580k/year (approx +20%)- Discount: tiered per-token discounts that yield ~12% blended savings vs their current published per-token rate- Renewal uplift cap: 10% max list-price increase year-over-year (contract clause)- Underutilization: 1 quarter rollover; option to right-size at renewal with pro-rated credit for unused committed spend beyond 90% utilization- Deal mechanics: 12-month term, 60-day notice for right-sizing at renewal

Option B — Growth-aligned- Commit: $624k/year (approx +30%)- Discount: deeper tiering with a step-down at 30%+ usage producing ~18% blended savings- Renewal uplift cap: 15% max list-price increase year-over-year (requires approval from pricing desk)- Underutilization: up to two quarters rollover, 50% of unused annual commit eligible for credit at renewal (subject to minimum landed ARR)- Additional: an optional ‘burst pool’ for 3 months at list price if they spike >1.5x usage

Questions for legal/pricing:
- Are we comfortable with 15% uplift cap for a 3-year commitment?
- Any precedent on 50% crediting for unused commit at renewal? Last time we did crediting it was closer to 25%.
- Could we add a usage guardrail clause with a monthly reconciliation to prevent credit gaming?

I’ll mark up the contract template once we land on terms. Thoughts?

Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Olivia — attaching two firm proposals based on our conversations and internal calibration. High level summary below and attachments. Let me know which option you want to take to a procurement/finance review; we can schedule a call next week to walk the numbers.

Summary: 
Option 1 (Conservative)- Annual commit: $585,000- Effective per-token: $0.00083 (blended)- Renewal uplift cap: 10% year-over-year- Rollover: 1 quarter allowed; pro-rated credit at renewal for unused commit beyond 90% utilization

Option 2 (Growth-aligned)- Annual commit: $624,000- Effective per-token: $0.00077 (blended)- Renewal uplift cap: 15% year-over-year (requires pricing desk sign-off)- Rollover: up to 2 quarters; up to 50% of unused annual commit eligible for credit at renewal (conditional on minimum ARR and usage guardrails)

Additional notes: both proposals include a 3-month burst pool at list price and a monthly reconciliation process to avoid credit gaming. We also included an appendix showing how blended per-token numbers were calculated from their current usage profile.
